body:
## Problem
A dormant VTuber session that resumed without a valid \`chat_room_id\` used to **create a fresh empty room** in \`_rehydrate\`. That stranded the real conversation behind an empty duplicate — the chat panel then showed "대화를 시작해보세요" even though the full history was intact in the DB.

Confirmed on prod: tester session \`eb5aef2f-…\` had two rooms — \`decf8c75-…\` (46 messages, real) and \`a5549dc4-…\` (0 messages, the orphan the old logic created). The session's \`chat_room_id\` pointed at the empty one.

## Fix
\`_rehydrate\` now **reconciles** to the session's best existing room — the one with the most messages (tiebreak: most recently updated) among rooms that list the session — and only creates a new room when the session has none at all.

- add \`AgentSessionManager._best_chat_room_for(session_id)\`
- rewrite the ensure-chat-room block to reconcile, not always-create
- test: prefers the message-bearing room over the empty dup

This **auto-recovers** conversations orphaned by the earlier logic on next resume (no manual DB surgery needed) and prevents future orphaning.

## Test

author: marcschier
body:
# Description

This PR also renames the project itself from `Opc.Ua.Bindings.Pcap` (assembly / NuGet / folder / root namespace) to `Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics`. `Pcap`-prefixed type names (`PcapFileWriter`, `PcapOptions`, `IPcapAuditSink`, ...) and the `AddPcap*` extension methods are preserved — only the project shell broadens to `Core.Diagnostics`. The new NuGet id is `OPCFoundation.NetStandard.Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics`. Folders were moved with `git mv` so blame and log are preserved.

This PR also renames the **C# namespace** from `Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics.*` to `Opc.Ua.Pcap.*` (commit `efc03691c`). The **assembly identity** stays `Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics` (assembly name, NuGet id `OPCFoundation.NetStandard.Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics`, folder, csproj filename, `InternalsVisibleTo`, .slnx project paths, sign-lists are all unchanged). Result: one `Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics.dll` assembly hosting types in the `Opc.Ua.Pcap.*` namespace — standard .NET pattern (cf. `System.Net.Http.dll` hosting `System.Web.*`). Future diagnostic features can add other `Opc.Ua.*` namespaces to the same assembly without another rename. 149 files changed (+411/-411 net); 422/422 tests pass on net10.0.

This PR also merges `Docs/PacketCapture.md` and `Docs/Observability.md` into a new `Docs/Diagnostics.md`. `ITelemetryContext` leads the doc with expanded usage and extensibility guidance (custom contexts, OpenTelemetry exporter wiring, ActivitySource / Meter naming conventions, testing patterns). New sections cover OPC UA server audit events and the built-in `Server.ServerDiagnostics` info-model nodes. The 1.4 / 1.5 evolution narrative has been dropped; the still-relevant migration content has moved into `Docs/MigrationGuide.md`. All 8 inbound doc / slnx / XML-doc references are retargeted.

This PR also adds a new public DI extension `AddPcapFromEnvironment` to `OPCFoundation.NetStandard.Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics` that activates packet capture and/or symmetric-key logging at host start based on two environment variables. The variables are evaluated **once** during the `AddXXX` call (matching the existing `OPCUA_PCAP_ENABLE_DIAGNOSTICS` opt-in semantics):

| Variable | Effect when set |
|---|---|
| `OPCUA_PCAP_FILE` | Auto-start an in-process capture session on host start. Frames are written verbatim to the literal path; the parent directory becomes `PcapOptions.BaseFolder` so the existing `SessionFolder` path-traversal validation still runs. |
| `OPCUA_KEYLOGFILE` | When set without `OPCUA_PCAP_FILE`: install a stand-alone keylog observer (SSLKEYLOGFILE-style) directly into `IChannelCaptureRegistry`. When set together with `OPCUA_PCAP_FILE`: keylog records go to this path instead of the conventional `*.uakeys.json` sibling of the pcap. |

When neither variable is set the call behaves exactly like `AddPcap` — binding registered, no auto-start. When the auto-start path is active the host emits a `Warning`-level log line naming the env var(s) consumed and the resolved path(s); key material is never logged.

## Public surface

The new public API is intentionally narrow:

```csharp
namespace Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics.DependencyInjection
{
    public static class PcapEnvironmentVariableNames
    {
        public const string OpcuaPcapFile = "OPCUA_PCAP_FILE";
        public const string OpcuaKeyLogFile = "OPCUA_KEYLOGFILE";
    }

    public static partial class PcapServiceCollectionExtensions
    {
        public static IServiceCollection AddPcapFromEnvironment(this IServiceCollection services);
        public static IServiceCollection AddPcapFromEnvironment(this IServiceCollection services, Action<PcapOptions> configure);
    }
}
```

`StandaloneKeyLogObserver`, `PcapEnvironmentDefaults`, and `PcapEnvironmentAutoStartHostedService` are internal — the env-var names and DI methods are the only public surface, which keeps it AOT-clean.

## Behaviour-impacting code change

`InProcessCaptureSourceBase` now honors `StartCaptureRequest.PcapFilePath` and `StartCaptureRequest.KeyLogFilePath` for in-process capture (previously these properties were respected only by the Replay source, despite their generic XML docs). Behaviour is **opt-in**: callers that pass `null` continue to get the conventional `capture.pcap` / `keys.uakeys.json` / `keys.uakeys.txt` filenames inside `SessionFolder`. Path-traversal validation in `CaptureSessionManager.StartAsync` is unchanged.

## Operator example

```yaml
# Kubernetes manifest snippet
env:
  - name: OPCUA_PCAP_FILE
    value: /var/log/opcua/cap.pcap
  - name: OPCUA_KEYLOGFILE
    value: /var/log/opcua/keys.uakeys.json
```

```csharp
// Program.cs
HostApplicationBuilder builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder();
builder.Services.AddOpcUa().AddClient(_ => { });
builder.Services.AddPcapFromEnvironment();
await builder.Build().RunAsync();
```

For SSLKEYLOGFILE-style keylog only (no pcap):

```bash
export OPCUA_KEYLOGFILE=$HOME/opcua-keys.uakeys.json
```

## Security model

Anyone (process, container runtime, host operator, sidecar) who can set these env vars can divert OPC UA channel keys and traffic to attacker-controlled paths. `Docs/PacketCapture.md` gains a security note and an operator-checklist item that ties this to the existing security guidance: the destination path / directory must be operator-controlled and protected with file-system permissions in addition to the binding's own `0600`-on-Unix file mode.

## Related Issues

_No tracking issue — this is an additive convenience feature on top of the existing capture binding._

- Fixes _none_

## Checklist

- [x] I have signed the [CLA](https://opcfoundation.org/license/cla/ContributorLicenseAgreementv1.0.pdf) and read the [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/OPCFoundation/UA-.NETStandard/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) doc.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works and increased code coverage.
  - 35 new NUnit tests across `StandaloneKeyLogObserverTests`, `PcapEnvironmentDefaultsTests`, `PcapEnvironmentAutoStartHostedServiceTests`, `AddPcapFromEnvironmentTests`, and `InProcessCaptureSourceExplicitPathsTests`. Full `Tests/Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics.Tests` suite 422/422 on `net10.0`.
- [x] I have added all necessary documentation.
  - New “Environment-variable configuration” section in `Docs/PacketCapture.md` with usage examples (Kubernetes, SSLKEYLOGFILE-style, both env vars set), defaults-table rows, security note, and operator-checklist item.
- [x] I have verified that my changes do not introduce (new) build or analyzer warnings.
  - `Stack/Opc.Ua.Core.Diagnostics` builds 0 warnings / 0 errors on `net8.0`, `net9.0`, and `net10.0`. `Applications/McpServer` (a downstream consumer) also builds clean.
- [ ] I ran **all** tests locally using the **UA.slnx** solution against at least .net **framework** and .net **10**, and all passed.
  - Full Pcap-binding tests pass on `net10.0`. Solution-wide UA.slnx run is pending (the binding multi-targets net8/9/10 only; legacy CI runs strip the project to a no-op shell via `RestrictForLegacyTfm` so net48 is not affected). Reviewer guidance welcome on whether the full UA.slnx run is required given this scoping.
- [ ] I fixed **all** failing and flaky tests in the CI pipelines and **all** CodeQL warnings.

## Summary

Adds ADR-0058, which retires the inherited paired dev/user doc convention now that PRISM is its own single-audience product. The supersession is deliberately scoped, not blanket:

- **ADR-0038** (paired-dev-doc gates) — superseded **wholesale**.
- **ADR-0023** (architect-docs source-verified review) — only its **paired-dev-doc clause** is retired; its `.prism/architect/**` source-verification gate survives.
- **ADR-0044** (direct-write tool outputs) — only its **paired-doc obligation** (`compatibility.md` companion) is retired; its direct-write / `.generated`-collapse spine survives.

## What did you do?

Authored `0058-single-audience-retires-paired-dev-docs.md`, dual-written byte-identically to the canonical (`.prism/`) and templates (`templates/install/.prism/`) trees. Flipped ADR-0038's status to `superseded` (with `Superseded-by: 0058`) and added scoped `Superseded-in-part-by: 0058` frontmatter plus a top-of-doc note to ADR-0023 and ADR-0044 naming exactly which clause dies and which survives. Updated the ADR index (README) in both trees and allowlisted ADR-0058's load-bearing Thrive reference in the literal guard. Appended a PR-2 line to the Epic A plan's `## History`.

## Why did you do it?

The paired-doc clauses were correct for Thrive's Nextra/block setting — two genuinely distinct audiences read each decision through different lenses. The context changed when PRISM became its own product: it has one audience (the developer-user), the architect doc *is* the thing they read, and doc format/placement is now a per-team onboarding output (Atlas), not a PRISM-mandated path. Maintaining a second synced copy of every decision buys nothing once the two audiences collapse into one. This is a context shift, not a correction.

## How did you achieve it?

The supersession lifecycle followed the ADR README: status carries state, frontmatter carries the link. Wholesale supersession (0038) flips `Status` to `superseded`; partial supersession (0023, 0044) keeps `accepted` — both ADRs are still in force for their surviving halves — and uses a clearly-named `Superseded-in-part-by` field plus an inline note rather than overwriting the historical body. Platform mirrors (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.cursor/`) were regenerated by `pnpm prism:build`; the literal guard required an allowlist entry for the legitimate Thrive-context citation, matching the existing pattern for ADR-0038/0044.

body:
## Bug (Low, source review L4)

`_count_amino_acids` counted over `sequence.upper()`. A letter whose uppercase form is multiple characters (e.g. the German eszett -> "SS") expands one input character into two counted residues, breaking the length invariant and inventing residues — corrupting length, MW, GRAVY, aromaticity, and composition.

Reachability via the shipped tools is negligible (UniProt FASTA is ASCII and `compute_protein_properties` is not re-exported from the package `__init__`); the trigger is a direct library call with exotic non-ASCII input or a malformed upstream payload.

## Fix

Uppercase each character individually rather than the whole string. A multi-character uppercasing then no longer matches a single amino-acid key and falls to the existing "other" bucket, preserving the length invariant. ASCII sequences are unchanged.

## Verification

- New test `test_multichar_uppercase_letter_falls_to_other`: `"A" + eszett + "A"` yields length 2, two Ala, zero Ser, one "other", and the expected MW (2x Ala residue mass + water, ExPASy/IUPAC constants — independent of code output).
- Fail-on-unfixed verified: reverting only the source edit makes the test go RED (`assert 4 == 2` — the eszett expands to "SS").
- Full offline suite: 874 passed, 45 skipped, 100% line+branch coverage. `ruff` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy --strict` clean.

Produced under a full re-derivation of every molecular constant in `proteinchem.py` (residue masses, water, Kyte-Doolittle, aromaticity, pKa/pI, cystine=125) against authoritative references; **no second wrong constant** was found beyond C1 (#73). The counting loop is a different region from the C1 extinction fix, so this is independent of #73.

body:
## Contexte

Permettre d'**essayer Arty sans compte Google ni CB**. Identité = email vérifié par code OTP. Réutilise l'infra trial existante (cap 30 messages), avec un **espace de clés disjoint** pour ne jamais collisionner avec les comptes Google.

Conçu après un **audit red-team à 3 agents en parallèle** (RÈGLE 7) : red-team sécu (Opus), vérif terrain (Sonnet), challenge archi (Sonnet). Le design initial (OTP simple + jeton HMAC stateless) a été jugé **non sûr** ; cette PR intègre les **9 correctifs bloquants** identifiés.

### Décisions d'architecture issues de l'audit
- **OTP 6 chiffres, pas magic-link** : un lien email ouvre Chrome au lieu de la WebView sur APK (BUG 53 en pire) → OTP garde la même session sur web / PWA / APK.
- **Jeton de session opaque en D1, pas HMAC stateless** : 256 bits, stocké **hashé**, **révocable** ligne par ligne (logout). Pas de rotation catastrophique, pas de jeton 30 j irrévocable.

## Sécurité — correctifs bloquants intégrés

| # | Risque | Fix |
|---|--------|-----|
| **CRIT-1** | Collision d'identité (OTP hérite du plan premium / mémoire d'un compte Google du même email) | Table dédiée `email_trial_usage` + identité préfixée `trial-email:<email>` ; plan **figé `trial`**, **jamais** `resolveUserPlan`/`ALLOWED_EMAILS` ; `verifyGoogleUser` **non élargi** → la mémoire reste Google-only |
| **CRIT-2** | Hash OTP nu crackable hors-ligne | `HMAC(EMAIL_TRIAL_SECRET, email‖code)` |
| **CRIT-3** | OTP prédictible (`Math.random`) | `crypto.getRandomValues` + rejection sampling |
| **HIGH-3** | Race / double-spend sur la vérif | Mono-statement atomique `DELETE … RETURNING` |
| **HIGH-1/2/5** | Brute-force, « 1 code N comptes », email-bombing, Map in-memory par isolat | Rate-limit **D1 fail-closed** (5/email/jour, 10/IP/h, 30 verifs/IP/h) + 5 essais/code + Turnstile optionnel |
| **HIGH-6** | Bypass `+alias` / points Gmail / jetables | `normalizeEmail` (strip alias + points Gmail) + blacklist domaines jetables |

**Audit sécu (RÈGLE 6)** — 3 endpoints créés :
- **Authn** : request-otp sans auth par nature → rate-limit fail-closed + Turnstile (si configuré). verify-otp = possession OTP, atomique, capé. Gate proxy = Google (audience `aud` validée) OU jeton d'essai vérifié.
- **Authz** : email-trial = plan `trial` figé, espace de clés disjoint → pas d'escalade premium, pas d'accès cross-user.
- **Abus infra** : email-bombing/Resend bornés ; secrets serveur-only (RÈGLE 1, jamais `VITE_`).
- **Leak** : réponses uniformes (`invalid_code` indistinct expiré/faux/trop d'essais) ; pas d'`ACAO:*`.
- **Origin/CSRF** : middleware inchangé (POST exige Origin whitelisté).

## Changements

**Serveur** — `functions/api/_lib/emailTrial.ts` (cœur), endpoints `auth/email/{request-otp,verify-otp,logout}`, gate des 4 proxys IA (Google OU jeton d'essai ; épuisé → 403 direct, jamais de wallet), `env.d.ts` (+`RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `EMAIL_TRIAL_SECRET`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`), middleware (header `x-arty-trial-token`).

**Client** — `emailTrialClient.ts` (jeton scopé par userId), `EmailTrialFlow.tsx` (email → code), injection `x-arty-trial-token` dans les 4 clients chat, `useAuth.logout` révoque + supprime le jeton (BUG 41), onboarding « Essayer avec mon email » + splash trial réutilisé, i18n FR/EN.

## Vérifs
- `tsc --noEmit` (src **+** functions) : ✅ exit 0
- `vitest` : ✅ **429 tests** (12 nouveaux : normalisation anti-abus, format OTP CSPRNG, clé disjointe)
- Rebasé proprement sur `main` à jour (au-dessus de #292 durcissement OAuth `aud` — `resolveProxyIdentity` aligné sur la nouvelle signature `verifyGoogleUser(request, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID)`).

## Ops requis avant activation (Cloudflare Pages)
- `RESEND_API_KEY` (déjà utilisé par le growth-orchestrator) + **domaine vérifié** chez Resend + `EMAIL_FROM` (ex. `Arty <noreply@tryarty.com>`)
- `EMAIL_TRIAL_SECRET` : secret aléatoire ≥32 chars
- ⚠️ **Ne PAS définir `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`** tant que le widget Turnstile client n'est pas ajouté (sinon request-otp échouerait) — les rate-limits D1 assurent le plancher d'ici là. Widget = follow-up.

## À tester par Florent (impossible en conteneur)
- Round-trip réel : saisie email → réception du code Resend → vérif → chat (Haiku) → compteur trial décrémente → épuisé à 30 → 403 propre.
- APK + PWA : que la session tient bien (pas de bascule navigateur).

author: ready22race
body:
## Problem

When the host gracefully stops (SIGTERM), it tears down the agent subprocess while a turn may still be in flight. The SDK then raises a **transport/process death** rather than a task error:

- **codex** — `TransportClosedError` ("Codex process closed stdout"), and a follow-up write to the dead stdin surfaces as `BrokenPipeError`
- **socket/stdio transports** generally — `ConnectionError` (which `BrokenPipeError` / `ConnectionResetError` subclass) or `EOFError`

All three runtimes stamped these as `execution_error` and emitted a scary `session_error`. This made graceful shutdown behave **worse than a hard kill**:

| Shutdown kind | Session row left as | Recovery outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Hard kill (SIGKILL / OOM) | `running` → `scan_orphan_runs` flips to `host_restart` | **resumed** ✅ |
| Graceful stop (SIGTERM) | runtime stamps `execution_error` | member marked terminal → **archived** ❌ |

Observed in the field: a task whose turn was in flight at app-quit ended with the lead `stop_reason = execution_error "[Errno 32] Broken pipe"` and its member `archived`, instead of resuming on next launch.

## Fix

Add `is_runtime_interruption(exc)` (new `kernel/src/runtimes/interruption.py`) and gate the `except Exception` block in the **codex / claude_agent / deepagents** runtimes:

- A transport/process death → resumable **`interrupted`** stop_reason, with the `session_error` event **and** the `on_error` hook suppressed.
- A genuine task failure → unchanged `execution_error` + error card.

`classify_member` (host recovery) now treats `interrupted` as resumable **alongside** `host_restart`, so boot recovery re-drives the turn exactly like the hard-kill path. `RESUME_RETRY_CAP` remains the backstop for a subprocess that dies on every attempt.

## Why this complements #133

#133 (already merged) flips a host-side **draining** flag on shutdown so the task actor loop skips `_finalize_actor`, keeping the task `active` and the session `running` for boot recovery. This change is the runtime-side half:

- It makes the **lost turn resumable rather than failed**, so the member is re-driven instead of archived.
- It also covers a **kernel-only restart** that the host draining flag cannot see (the host stays up; only the kernel subprocess died).

## Tests

- `tests/runtimes/test_interruption.py` — `is_runtime_interruption` covers `TransportClosedError`, `BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionError`/`ConnectionResetError`, `EOFError` (True) and real failures `RuntimeError`/`ValueError`/`KeyError` (False).
- `tests/modules/tasks/test_recovery.py` — adds `test_classify_interrupted_is_resumable`.
- Full `tests/runtimes/` + `tests/modules/tasks/` suites pass (207). Ruff clean; no new mypy errors (host baseline unchanged).

body:
## Summary

Implements STORY-632 v1: deterministic spec **centrality/heft** materialized in the rebuildable SQLite cache (`.aida/cache.db`), computed from the relationship graph and surfaced on read. Never written to canonical YAML (same computed-not-stored principle as stale in STORY-631).

## What changed

- **Cache schema** (`cache_schema.sql`, v4 → v5): adds `in_degree`, `out_degree`, `heft` INTEGER columns + an index on `heft`. Existing caches auto-drop+rebuild on the version bump (the established STORY-441/BUG-485 migration path).
- **Degree computation** (`compute_degrees` in `cache.rs`): one pass over the full store's relationship graph. `out_degree` = a spec's own outbound edges; `in_degree` = edges from other specs targeting it — **tracked separately** (inbound = load-bearing heft; outbound = coupling). v1 = raw **local** degree, no transitive / PageRank.
- **Type-weighted heft**: static `RelationshipType -> weight` lookup (`edge_weight`) per the operator-agreed table — BlockedBy/Blocks 3, Parent/Child 2, Verifies/VerifiedBy/References/Custom 1, Duplicate 0 — summed over inbound + outbound edges. **No weight field added to `Relationship`**; the dormant `weight` field on `Requirement` is **untouched**.
- **Read surface**:
  - `aida show <ID>` prints a `Centrality: N in / M out  (heft H)` line (only when connected).
  - **new** `aida show --json` emits the spec as an object including `in_degree`/`out_degree`/`heft`.
  - MCP `build_summaries` mirrors the fields so the MCP projection matches the cache.
- **`aida list --sort heft`** (nice-to-have, shipped): orders most-connected first (`--sort modified` default; unknown values warn + fall back).

## Notes / followups

- Single-row write-through (`upsert_requirement`) keeps the touched row's own **outbound** axis fresh and **preserves** its inbound axis; a neighbor's edge change re-derives inbound only on the next full `aida cache rebuild` — same rebuildable-projection contract as the rest of the cache. Documented inline.
- STORY-631 intent-pass consumer link (feeding heft + heaviest-neighbor names into the intent prompt) is **not** in this PR to keep scope tight — raw degree in cache + show/json is the core deliverable. Follow-up.

## Tests

- `compute_degrees_counts_inbound_and_outbound_separately` — synthetic star graph (N inbound + M outbound → in=N, out=M, heft = weighted sum).
- `edge_weight_table_matches_agreed_values` — the static weight table.
- `cache_roundtrips_degree_columns` — rebuild → `degrees_for_id` round-trip + unknown-id default.

author: hyoshi
body:
Fixes #273 (CRITICAL — silent customer-data destruction).

## Problem
`meta_ads_ad_sets_update` passed the supplied `targeting` dict straight to Meta via `json.dumps`. Meta **replaces the entire targeting spec** on write, so an agent intending a partial change (e.g. `{"age_min": 25}`) silently cleared `geo_locations`, `custom_audiences`, `interests`, placements, etc. on a live, real-spend ad set. Same shape as the logly-bridge incident (collection full-replacement → data loss). The tool description correctly warned "fetch and merge" but no merge path existed in code.

## Fix
- `update_ad_set` now does a **read-modify-write by default**: when `targeting` is a dict, it `get_ad_set()`s the current spec and shallow-merges the supplied top-level keys over it (`_merge_targeting`). Omitted keys are preserved.
- New keyword-only `replace_targeting: bool = False` escape hatch for deliberate whole-spec replacement (e.g. to clear a facet); when true, no read is performed.
- Handler `handle_ad_sets_update` passes `replace_targeting` through.
- Tool description rewritten to "merge-by-default", documents `replace_targeting`, and corrects the false "reversible via rollback_apply" claim to "not automatically reversible".

Merge granularity is top-level only — a supplied key replaces that key wholesale (nested lists like `flexible_spec` are not deep-merged, which would be ambiguous).

## Tests (TDD)
- `test_update_ad_set_targeting_merges_with_existing` — unrelated keys survive a partial delta (the regression guard).
- `test_update_ad_set_targeting_delta_overrides_key` — a supplied top-level key wins.
- `test_update_ad_set_targeting_merge_no_existing_spec` — no existing spec falls back to `{}` (no crash).
- `test_update_ad_set_targeting_replace_bypasses_merge` — `replace_targeting=True` skips the read and replaces wholesale.

## Verification
- AdSetsMixin 14 tests + related regression (234) pass; ruff/black/mypy clean on changed files.
- code-reviewer: approved, no CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM.

## Notes
- `test_mcp_server::test_list_tools_returns_all_tools` (331≠185) fails only in the local editable-install env due to discovered plugin tools — pre-existing, unrelated (this PR adds a property, not a tool; Meta tool count unchanged).

Adds the stdio/long-lived-connection half of dual-era serving: `ServerOptions.eraSupport` with a `'legacy'` default that preserves today's behavior exactly, per-message era selection on dual-era connections via a protocol-layer classification consult, the era gate that keeps 2026-only methods invisible to 2025-era traffic, era-keyed direction enforcement, and a runnable dual-era stdio example with real child-process e2e coverage.

## Motivation and Context
The 2026-07-28 draft revision can already be served over HTTP per request (`createMcpHandler`). stdio servers are different: they are hand-constructed, long-lived, and bound to one connection — so serving the new revision there has to be a per-message decision on the same pipe, and it has to be impossible to change what an existing server puts on the wire just by upgrading the SDK.

- **`ServerOptions.eraSupport: 'legacy' | 'dual-era' | 'modern'`** (default `'legacy'`). The default changes nothing: no `server/discover`, no new advertisement, byte-identical 2025 serving. `'dual-era'` serves both eras on one connection, classifying each message by the per-request `_meta` envelope (`initialize` and claim-less messages are 2025-era; envelope-carrying messages are 2026-era) — one option, transport unchanged. `'modern'` is strict 2026-only: requests without the envelope (including `initialize`) get the unsupported-protocol-version error with the supported list.
- **A 2026-era revision in `supportedProtocolVersions` now requires the declaration**: on a default instance it throws a `TypeError` at construction instead of silently installing the discover handler.
- **Protocol-layer classification consult**: a new protected `Protocol._classifyInbound` hook, consulted only when the transport did not classify a message (an HTTP-edge classification always wins). The server override classifies per message on declared instances; the base implementation returns `undefined`, leaving every existing dispatch path untouched.
- **Era gate on long-lived connections**: methods that exist in only one era stay invisible to the other — a 2025-era request for `server/discover` (or any 2026-only method) answers the same plain `-32601` a 2025 server sends, with nothing in the message or data revealing the modern registry; a 2026-era request for a removed method answers `-32601` too, and outbound requests die locally with a typed error when the era does not define them.
- **Directionality**: the 2026 era has no server→client JSON-RPC request channel. A `'modern'` server cannot emit sampling/elicitation/roots wire requests; a dual-era server still can toward the 2025-era clients it serves; and a client whose connection negotiated a modern era drops inbound requests instead of answering them (on stdio the client must never write responses).
- **Accessors on dual-era instances**: `getClientCapabilities()` / `getClientVersion()` / `getNegotiatedProtocolVersion()` keep their `initialize`-scoped semantics and are never backfilled from 2026-era requests (mixed-era interleaving makes instance-level backfill racy); handlers read per-request identity from `ctx.mcpReq.envelope`. Documented in the migration guide.
- **Demo + e2e**: `examples/server/src/dualEraStdio.ts` (the opt-in is the single option; the transport line is unchanged) with a two-legged client example, plus an integration suite that spawns the same server shape as a real child process and drives the 2025 vertical, the 2026 vertical negotiated via `server/discover` on the pipe, and the era-gate negative on one connection. Stdio has no conformance harness, so this SDK e2e coverage is its referee.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- New unit suites for the per-message era predicate (including the rule that classification keys on the reserved protocol-version `_meta` key, never bare `_meta`), the classification consult (edge classification always wins; the base path is unchanged; per-message era on dual-era instances; strict-instance handoff; the drop arm), `eraSupport` construction/serving semantics, the long-lived era gate with a dedicated zero-2026-vocabulary leak test, a scripted-2025 golden pin on a default server, the client-side inbound-request drop, and a merged first-contact fixture corpus for the probe classifier (probe edges plus the wire shapes deployed 2025 servers actually answer).
- A real child-process stdio integration suite covering both eras and the era gate on one pipe, plus the runnable examples.
- Full repo gates: typecheck, lint, build, docs build, every package suite, integration, the full e2e matrix, and the conformance suites against the published referee with no expected-failures changes.

## Breaking Changes
One deliberate, narrow break (changeset + migration entry): constructing a `Server`/`McpServer` with a 2026-era revision in `supportedProtocolVersions` without declaring `eraSupport` now throws a `TypeError` (previously it silently installed the `server/discover` handler). Servers that do not opt in are byte-identical to before, and the default version list is unaffected.

## Types of changes
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist
- [x] I have read the [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have added or updated documentation as needed

## Additional context
- The classification consult is deliberately the only change to the protocol dispatch file; everything era-specific lives in the role classes and the existing classification pure module.
- Typed client-side decoding of cacheable list results (e.g. `tools/list`) on the 2026 era completes once result stamping supplies the required cache fields; until then the modern list leg is exercised at the wire level and the example uses `tools/call`.

Stands up the deterministic plumbing for **Balloon Squeeze** (Roadmap Phase 0).

## What's here
- **`bsq.llm`** — provider-agnostic `LLMClient` protocol + `make_client()`; an offline, **deterministic** `MockClient` (seeded, no network/key). Real providers are stubbed behind the same interface for later phases.
- **`bsq.models`** — `Persona`, `Proposition` (checkable/uncheckable + placebo-irrelevant), `Claim`, `Agent`, `VerifierArm`, `Game`, `GameConfig`, and the five standard verifier arms (`A0_off`, `A1_announced`, `A1_implicit`, `A2_silent`, `A3_placebo`). Engine holds ground truth; it never enters a prompt.
- **`bsq.config`** — `BSQ_*` env parsing with fail-fast boundary validation.
- **`bsq.events`** — append-only event bus (the data artifact); emitted payloads are read-only.
- **`bsq.cli`** — `bsq selftest` runs a zero-setup determinism check on mock.

## Tooling (modern conventions)
`src/` layout · hatchling build · `requires-python >=3.11` · ruff (lint+imports) · mypy `--strict` · pytest. The core/`mock` path is **dependency-free** so it runs and tests offline.

- [x] `ruff check .` clean

body:
**⚠️ GATED — careful review requested.** This touches the **data layer** (`consume_yarn` / `grant_yarn` RPCs) **and the core card-open flow**. It's a faithful port of the PWA yarn module (`web_pwa/public/m/assets/m-app.js`, yarn section ~4485+). **No new SQL** — `06_yarn.sql` already ships `consume_yarn`, `grant_yarn`, and `users.yarn_balance`.

## How the gate works (read this first)
On opening a card (`CardDetailView.runOpenFlow`), in PWA `openDetail` order:
1. **Reward first** — `rewardFirstOpen(cardId)` grants **+1** once per card (local dedup via `ds.yarnRewarded`). Doing this *before* the gate means a **first-ever open self-funds** (+1 then −1 = net 0, card unlocked 3 days).
2. **Gate** — `gateOpen(cardId:tourActive:)`:
   - card **unlocked** (opened within the last **3 days**, `ds.yarnUnlocked`) → **free**
   - **coach tour active** → free *(see flag #4 — no iOS tour yet, so always false)*
   - else **`consume_yarn`**: success → mark unlocked + open; **−1 (insufficient)** → **blocked**: an opaque gate overlay covers the card (no reveal, no view-count) and offers **충전하러 가기** → purchase sheet.

Net effect: **new/first opens never lock** (the +1 funds them); the block only bites when **re-opening a card whose 3-day unlock expired and that was already rewarded, at 0 balance** — the intended monetization pressure.

## What's included
| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `SupabaseClient` | `consumeYarn() -> Int` (`-1` = insufficient), `grantYarn(_:) -> Int` (`p_n`); `yarn_balance` added to the users select |
| `UserRow` / `AuthSession` | `yarnBalance` loaded at bootstrap |
| `YarnStore` (`@MainActor`) | single UI source for balance; local 3-day unlock + rewarded maps; `gateOpen`, `rewardFirstOpen`, `grant(_:)` |
| `CardDetailView` | reward + gate on open; opaque insufficient overlay |
| `YarnPurchaseView` + `YarnChip` | tiers `[1/100, 10/1000, 21/2000, 32/3000, 113/10000]`, "준비 중" banner, mock `grant_yarn` (no StoreKit); chip in `AppMasthead` opens the sheet |

Tiers, the 3-day window, and the `ds.yarnUnlocked` / `ds.yarnRewarded` keys match the PWA exactly.

## 🚩 Flags / decisions for the reviewer
1. **The gate is re-activated for all card opens (incl. anonymous users).** In the **current PWA, `spendYarn` has no callers** — the open gate is effectively *off* there; only the +1 reward runs. This PR implements the gate per the task spec. **Confirm this is the intended product behavior** before merge.
2. **First-open reward uses `grant_yarn(1)` + LOCAL dedup**, not the PWA's server-deduped `reward_yarn_first_view` (which *does* exist — `upload_web/supabase/migrations/035_yarn_card_rewards.sql`). Per the task ("add only `consume_yarn`/`grant_yarn`, track locally via `ds.yarnRewarded`", no new SQL) I kept it local. **Tradeoff: local-only dedup re-grants +1 on reinstall / new device.** Recommend a follow-up to switch to `reward_yarn_first_view` for durable dedup.
3. **`consume_yarn` network error → fail-open** (card opens, no charge, no unlock-mark) to avoid hard-locking a reader on a transient blip. Easy to flip to fail-closed if preferred.
4. **No iOS coach tour exists yet**, so `tourActive` is hardcoded `false`. The hook is in place for when the tour lands.
5. **Balance = server `users.yarn_balance` only** — the old 5/day free allotment is intentionally **not** reintroduced. `YarnStore.balance` is the single UI source: seeded from `AuthSession.yarnBalance` at bootstrap + on `userId` change, then updated from each RPC's returned balance.
6. **Attendance (+5)** UI is a later PR — `YarnStore.grant(_:)` is the exposed hook.

## Verify
- `xcodebuild -scheme Curtaincall -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build` → **BUILD SUCCEEDED** (incremental). No sim/screenshots — left to Codex.
- iOS only; no `web_pwa/`, Android, SQL, or `Config.swift`.

**Codex:** sim-test the open → gate → reward → purchase flow. Suggested cases: (a) fresh 0-balance user opens a new card (should open via the +1 self-fund); (b) re-open same card within 3 days (free); (c) force insufficient (e.g. open a 2nd brand-new card after the unlock map is cleared) → gate overlay → purchase → re-open succeeds; (d) chip balance updates after purchase/consume.
